title: After some inspiration to continue
author: Exetorius85
selftext:
I have been working on my game project for almost 12 months now. It has lived in my head rent free since I played X-Com Apocalypse waaaaaaaaaaaay back. I started out with the hard rule that I would only use AI to be my coding assistant / Git lackey....

That soon turned into me "architecting" the game code and I am now on the opposite side of my own rule where I use Claude to write the code under my instruction and rulesets, it then gets run through automations and negative tests before I play test every single feature and then tweak until its at a level I am satisfied with.

The reason I am here now.... I am not anti-ai, nor am I fully pro-ai.. I am confused, and I am looking for someone to slap me and tell me its ok to work the way I am working, or not (I know it should be me, but I am spiralling).. I have a hard and fast rule of no ai generated art, but even now I am teetering cos that's the part that is now holding me back.

Has anyone else betrayed their own rules to expedite delivery of their dream game? I still follow the basis of if I cannot explain my codebase, or how the game works then I have failed. It all started because I happened to create what I believe is a niche in a genre that is asking for delivery of what I intend to deliver

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body:
Nothing to betray - There are no rules, except if you are in some "crate a game without AI" competition.

You could say that life is a competition, but if you can't enforce the rules so everyone is playing by them... Just do what you need to do.

Don't break any laws though. :)

replies.author: Exetorius85
replies.body:
Appreciate the input. I think my main concern is pouring all this effort in and it just getting written off as slop.

Its easy to fall in to the game of AI, and hell Opus can pump out some magic if I asked it to but I have kept it to small targetted fixes so far.. very easy to get tempted to go "finish this for me"!

comments.author: SeaBuilding3911
comments.body:
Do it!

If you do it to be rich and famous, then don’t

Otherwise: do it!

replies.author: Exetorius85
replies.body:
Rich and famous! HA! I mean, everyone in life wants to be wealthy enough to be comfortable right?

But the main thing is I want people to play the game, the version of X-Com that I envision!

comments.author: ProfanedArbiter
comments.body:
I'll tell you as an outsider looking in. 

There's a lot of people I care about that have lost jobs in creative spaces because of AI. These are people I love and when I think about playing a game and I see an AI attribution in the description I think of them. I think of what my kids are going to do when they've grown up and are looking to aspire to something and I wonder what the hell there will even be to *do* at all. 

That's normally enough to put a bad taste in my mouth about the project.

replies.author: Exetorius85
replies.body:
See this is where I kind of sit too. I don't know many that have lost their jobs because of it. But yeah I just kinda fell into the trap without realising.. until I did. I would say I still hand crafted a good 60-70% of the code, and its still early doors so easily reversible.   
  
I too have kids and I want to set them on the right path, but then the way the world is going its a gamble isnt it? Teach them the way I was brought up and they might get left behind in a world where all corporations favour AI engineers over all else.

replies.author: ProfanedArbiter
replies.body:
It's tough man. We're all scared. 

As far as teaching the kids, I see it this way. The explicit stated goal of the tech, like the explicit business case pitched to investors, is that it will replace humans. If the tech gets good enough, and I'm increasingly thinking that may happen, then I don't think having "AI" skills will really be a thing. 

Which was an easier skill to learn? Computer science and software-engineering, or agentic programming workflows? CS and math teach deeper skills around creativity and problem solving. What does deploying agents teach? 

I figure they'll probably get a lot more out of learning the "old fashioned way" then the new way since, frankly, I don't expect they'll be doing the "new" way a whole lot either. 

Thanks for drawing a line at GenAI for art, music, etc. That one stings the most. Best of luck with the game, best of luck with the family, hit me up when it's finished :)
